newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures end mixed, off early lows.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures end mixed, off early lows.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo gold futures ended mixed on Wednesday after lacklustre Christmas trade, but off early lows as the dollar firmed against the yen, traders said.
Gold prices ranged from two yen per gram lower to six yen firmer. Most-active benchmark December was flat at 1,347 yen.

"One feature in the market was that investors rolled over their positions from October to December. Except for that, trade was dominated by sporadic inter-month trade in line with the currency market," one trader said.
Spot gold was quoted at $368.60/369.10 at the Tokyo close, against $368.90/369.40 in New York on Tuesday.
Traders said they were tending to hold slightly bullish views on spot gold and yen-based futures.
"Spot gold appears to find a floor at $368, and year-end short-covering could lift gold up to $370," one trader said.
Platinum futures settled narrowly mixed while palladium futures settled slightly firmer.
Some traders reported December shipments of platinum group metals from Russia had been delayed by up to two weeks.
"Palladium prices were relatively resilient, helped by the Russian factor," one trader said. Uncertainty concerning the delay in Japan-Russia platinum talks remained, they said.
Platinum futures moved sideways in directionless trade.

One trader said Japan's platinum demand from the jewellery sector is unlikely to rise next year partly due to a scheduled hike in the consumption tax from April, and that has weakened buying interest in platinum.
Palladium futures ranged from one to three yen per gram firmer, with benchmark December flat at 430 yen.
Platinum futures ranged from two yen per gram lower to two firmer. Benchmark December was down two yen at 1,356 yen.
Benchmark December silver was 0.3 yen per 10 grams lower at 179.5 yen. -- K.Takagi, Tokyo Commodity Desk +81-3-3432-7431
